releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.17
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 12.17.0 adds `pnpm peers check --global`, dependency-group selectors and wildcards in `overrides`, and runtime, package manager, Cargo, and Python updates in `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update`. It also fixes files that other users could not read in Docker images, and repeat installs that missed changes to local dependencies.

### Minor Changes

- `pnpm peers check` now accepts `--global` (`-g`) to check globally installed packages. After a global install or update, the peer dependency warning now suggests `pnpm peers check -g` [#17504](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17504).

- `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update` now inspect and update package manager and runtime versions in `devEngines.packageManager`, `packageManager`, `devEngines.runtime`, `engines.runtime`, and `runtime:` dependencies. With `cargo.enabled` or `python.enabled`, `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update` also inspect and update Cargo dependencies in `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` and Python dependencies in `pyproject.toml` and `pylock.toml`.

- `overrides` selectors now support `:prod`, `:optional`, and `:peer` pseudo-selectors that target a single dependency group. They also support `*` wildcard patterns on parent and target package names. An override with a non-range value, such as `npm:` or `file:`, no longer adds a peer dependency to `dependencies`. Removing an optional dependency with `"-"` now also removes the duplicate entry from `dependencies` [#5391](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5391).

### Patch Changes

#### Installing packages

- Files that pnpm creates in a project now get the permissions the umask gives any new file, such as `0644`. Before, several of them were readable only by the user who ran pnpm, which broke Docker images that run as a different user [#17435](https://github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/17435).

  The fix applies to:

  - `node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`. A different user running `pnpm run` reinstalled the dependencies because it could not read this file.
  - `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
  - the files written by `pnpm deploy`
  - patch files from `pnpm patch-commit`
  - the lockfile restored by `pnpm dedupe --check`
  - the Cargo and Python files that pnpm writes

  When pnpm edits an existing file, the file keeps its permissions.

- `pnpm install` no longer writes broken dependency links when the project's `node_modules` is a symlink to another directory, such as another project's `node_modules`. The install reported success, but the links it wrote did not resolve [#17448](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17448).

- Commands installed with `pnpm add --global` now find the dependencies that pnpm hoists for their package. A package that loads a dependency it does not declare, such as a native addon's platform-specific package, failed with "Cannot find module". Reinstall such a package with `pnpm add --global` to update its existing command [#17503](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17503).

- When pnpm switches to the version a project

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 11.28.10
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 11.28.10 stops `pnpm store prune` from deleting other stores when `cacheDir` points to their parent directory. It also fixes globally installed commands that load hoisted dependencies, and repeat installs that missed changes to local dependencies.

### Patch Changes

#### Installing packages

* `pnpm store prune` preserves other stores and global package data when `cacheDir` points to their parent directory.

* Commands installed with `pnpm add --global` now find the dependencies that pnpm hoists for their package. A package that loads a dependency it does not declare, such as a native addon's platform-specific package, failed with "Cannot find module". Reinstall such a package with `pnpm add --global` to update its existing command [#17503](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17503).

* `pnpm prune --prod` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_EXDEV` when `node_modules` was copied from an earlier Docker build stage [#17424](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17424).

* `pnpm install` now retries a Node.js runtime zip download when the connection drops partway through. A download that still fails names its URL. Before, a single dropped connection ended the install with `terminated` [#17411](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17411).

* With the global virtual store, a change to a dependency of one package in a dependency cycle now gives every package in that cycle a new directory. Before, the other packages kept their directories and still linked the old copy of the changed package, so the project could load two copies of it [#17466](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17466).

  Packages in a dependency cycle, and packages that depend on one, move to new global virtual store directories once after this update. Those that run a build miss the side-effects cache once.

* `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#17402](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402).

* The Node.js `latest` selector now chooses the newest stable release [#17490](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17490).

* The standalone `@pnpm/exe` builds now embed Node.js 26.13.0.

#### Repeat installs and lockfiles

* `pnpm install` now resolves a local directory again after its `package.json` changes when an override or a package extension adds it to the dependencies of a registry package. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails on a lockfile that still records the old dependencies of such a directory [#17486](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17486).

* With `injectWorkspacePackages` and per-project lockfiles, `pnpm install` now updates a project's lockfile when a local tarball that an injected workspace project depends on is replaced. The project's lockfile kept the old version and integrity before.

* `pnpm install` now detects a change to a local tarball or directory that only a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook depends on. A rep

prs.title: perf(deps-restorer): stat a store file once for the hardlink mode check
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17500.

The umask check from pnpm/pnpm#3807 (`source_has_desired_mode`) stats the store file before every hardlink, in both `hardlink_file` and the `Auto` hardlink tier. A store file shared by many packages was stat'ed once per link: about 67k extra `statx` calls and 13-15% more system CPU on the reporter's offline install.

`source_has_desired_mode` now remembers a linkable answer per source path for the rest of the process, so each store file is stat'ed once. Only linkable answers are cached. A mismatched entry is copied, and the copy costs far more than the stat.

Trade-off: a store file whose mode changes after its first link in the same process (for example a bin's exec bit set through a hardlink) is still hardlinked afterwards. That is what every release before 12.8.0 did for every file. In a long-lived `@pnpm/napi` embedder the set grows with the number of distinct store files linked, like the per-install `VerifiedFilesCache`.

v11 is not affected: the regression is in the Rust hardlink path only.

Not measured locally with strace on the vitest fixture. The new unit test proves the second link skips the mode check, and fails with the cache disabled.

```text

prs.title: fix(deps-restorer): keep a project's own nested copy as its direct dependency
prs.author: arthur-fontaine
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17498.

Under `nodeLinker: hoisted`, when two workspace projects each hold a nested copy of the same snapshot, every repeat install imports one of them again. `importer_direct_deps` set a project's direct dependency to the first location of the snapshot anywhere in the tree, so the second project's direct dependency pointed at the first project's copy. Linking the direct dependencies then moved the second project's own copy to `.ignored_<name>` and put a symlink in its place. The next install's `package_present_at` rejects that symlink, imports the copy again, and the direct links replace it again.

This PR makes a project's direct dependency the copy the hoister placed in that project's own `node_modules`, when that copy holds the resolved snapshot. Otherwise the snapshot's first recorded location wins, as before. Package-id matches (own copy, then first location) come last, for a peer variant the hoister collapsed.

### Build scripts run in every copy

The hoisted linker ran a snapshot's lifecycle scripts only in its first recorded copy. The other projects' copies used to be symlinks to that copy, so they got its build output. Once each project keeps its own copy, they were left unbuilt: `run_pre_and_postinstall_scripts_in_a_workspace_with_hoisted_linker` failed on this PR's first push. `build_one_snapshot` now runs the scripts in every distinct copy, the first one first. Patches already reached every copy, and only the first copy seeds the side

prs.author: kairosci
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/tasks#225.

If a catalog entry is set to a dist-tag, `pnpm add` now saves the dependency as `catalog:` and leaves the entry as written, in both CLIs.

```yaml
catalogMode: prefer
catalog:
  foo: beta
```

| command | | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pnpm add foo@beta` | v12 | `^1.2.3` direct (strict: mismatch error) | `catalog:`, entry `beta` |
| `pnpm add foo@beta` | v11 | `catalog:`, entry rewritten to `1.2.3` | `catalog:`, entry `beta` |

The entry already says which tag to follow, so pinning it to today's version would stop it from following the tag.

**v12:** `decide_catalog_entry` reuses an entry that equals the dist-tag typed in the selector. Only an explicit tag that the registry resolved matches. A versionless re-add does not match an entry set to the configured default tag. A tag that `linkWorkspacePackages` resolves to a local package keeps its `workspace:` specifier.

**v11:** the rewrite came from the explicit-dist-tag pin added in pnpm/pnpm#13478 for `pnpm update foo@beta` on an entry set to a version. After the resolver swaps the catalog entry in as the wanted specifier, `getCatalogUpdatesOfProject` cannot tell a tag read from the catalog from one the user typed. prs.title: fix(runtime): prefer stable Node.js versions when resolving a range
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17516. A Node.js range such as `>=26.13` in `devEngines.runtime` resolved to `27.0.0-alpha.0.0.0`, because the resolver matches ranges with prereleases included and the alpha is the highest version in the release index. Both CLIs had the bug. pnpm/pnpm#17492 fixed the same thing for `latest`, this does it for ranges.

The resolver now picks the highest stable version that satisfies the range and only falls back to a prerelease when no stable version matches. So `>=27` still gets the alpha today, and ranges on the `rc` channel (`rc/10`) still resolve to rc builds.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Node.js version ranges are matched with prereleases included, so the
rc and nightly channels, where every entry is a prerelease, can satisfy
a plain range like `10`. On the release channel this made `>=26.13`
pick 27.0.0-alpha.0.0.0 over 26.13.0.

Resolving a range now prefers the highest stable version that satisfies
it and only falls back to the highest prerelease when no stable version
does. Listing versions (`pnpm env list --remote <range>`) is unchanged.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17516
```

prs.title: fix(cli): update Cargo dependencies declared as multi-line inline tables
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

The scheduled dependency update workflow failed on pnpm 12.17.0 ([run](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/actions/runs/41074141328/job/124125700977)):

```
× cannot update crate axum: its Cargo.toml dependency declaration is not a
│ string or single-line inline table
```

The root `Cargo.toml` declares `axum` as an inline table whose `features` array continues on later lines. The Cargo manifest editor only read the value on the key's line, so it rejected the declaration and aborted the whole `pnpm update`.

Bug only in v12: v11 does not update Cargo dependencies.

Verified:

## Squash Commit Body

```text
`pnpm update` located a Cargo dependency's value on its key's line only,
so an inline table whose `features` array continues on later lines was
rejected as "not a string or single-line inline table". The root
Cargo.toml declares axum that way, which broke the scheduled dependency
update workflow.

The value now extends to the inline table's matching closing brace,
skipping strings and comments, and the `version` lookup inside the
table skips comments too. Only the version string is rewritten, so the
rest of the declaration keeps its formatting.

prs.title: fix(cmd-shim): quote paths in POSIX shims
prs.author: kairosci
prs.body:
## Summary

Both CLIs put the target path and `NODE_PATH` entries into POSIX shell shims inside double quotes, with no escaping. A directory name containing `$(...)` or a backtick then ran a command when the bin started. A name containing `$` or `"` gave a wrong path. This PR single-quotes every interpolated path in the pnpm 11 and pnpm 12 shim generators. It also teaches the readers that decide whether an existing shim is current to parse both the new form and the legacy double-quoted form.

Closes pnpm/tasks#241.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Shell shims wrote paths into double quotes without escaping `$`, backticks,
`"` or `\`. Both generators now single-quote each interpolated path:

- target: `"$basedir_abs"/'<relative>'` (also `$basedir` and `$basedir_win`),
  or `'<absolute>'`.
- NODE_PATH: `export NODE_PATH='<entries>'` and
  `export NODE_PATH='<entries>':"$NODE_PATH"`. In pnpm 12, a relocatable
  entry becomes `"$basedir_abs"/'<relative>'`. Adjacent literal entries share
  one quoted word, so a shim without relocatable entries is byte-identical
  across the two CLIs. Both CLIs compare such shims byte for byte.

Readers:

- pnpm 11 `readShNodePath` and `readShRelativeTarget` parse the new
  single-quoted words and still accept the legacy double-quoted form.
- pnpm 12 `is_relocatable_shim` validates both the new NODE_PATH form and the
  legacy one, and requires every entry to resolve inside the root.
- pnpm 12 `is_sh_shim_basedir_anchor_current` reads the anchored ta
…(truncated)

## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17526.

With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, pnpm 12 skipped a dependency's build scripts in a project whose global virtual store slot another project had already built. When the build writes only outside its own package (a git hook installer writing into `INIT_CWD`), the side-effects cache row is empty, so nothing is restored either, and the second project never gets the effect. pnpm 11 runs the script again there.

The skip is `built_by_an_earlier_install` in `slot_to_build.rs`, added by pnpm/pnpm#16286. That PR described it as matching v11, but v11 derives `isBuilt` only from the side-effects cache row (`getFlatMap` in `store/create-cafs-store`). `safeToSkip` changes how files are imported into the shared slot, not `isBuilt`. The only other v11 skip is in `importIntoSlot`: a slot that carried `.pnpm-needs-build`, then lost it while this install waited for the slot lock. v12 keeps that wait in `slot_to_build` as before.

This PR removes the slot-level skip. A slot whose build left output in the package still skips through the side-effects `is_built` gate, as in v11.

- **The cost.** With `sideEffectsCache: false`, or for a build that changes nothing inside its package, every install into a fresh `node_modules` now runs the build again. pnpm 11 does the same. pnpm/tasks#242 plans to make skipping these the intended behavior in the next major version, with `sideEffectsCache.exclude` as the opt-out.

prs.author: samanyudas

## Summary

Related to pnpm/pnpm#17475.

`pnpm link <dir>` could write a dependency name that pnpm itself rejects. Once that happens, every later install in the project fails until someone edits `package.json` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` by hand.

- In pnpm v11, `pnpm link .` in a project without a `name` field links it under the name `"."`. The fallback is `path.basename` of the raw argument. This writes `".": "link:"` to `package.json` and `.: 'link:'` to the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` overrides. That is the same `"."` key reported in pnpm/pnpm#17475.
- In both CLIs, a target whose `name` field is not a valid package name gets written the same way. The templates in the reporter's repository are named `"mcp-use server"`, for example.

`pnpm add` already rejects such a name before it writes anything. `pnpm link` now does the same. Both CLIs check the name with the rule `pnpm add` uses and fail with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_DEPENDENCY_NAME` before they change either file.

`pnpm link` with several paths could also drop overrides in pnpm v11. Each path wrote `pnpm-workspace.yaml` on its own and at the same time, so a write that read the file early and finished last lost the others' entries. With four paths, 11.13.1 lost two overrides in 2 of 6 runs. v11 now writes every override in one update, as v12 already does. After the fix, 10 of 10 runs kept all four.

prs.title: fix(runtime): stop the node shim from looping on a global pnpmfile
prs.author: samanyudas
prs.body:
## Summary

In a project that pins a Node.js version pnpm has not downloaded yet, `node -v` and `pnpm install` hang when a `globalPnpmfile` is configured. Each one fails after 30 seconds with `pnpmfile hook ... timed out` and leaves orphaned `node` workers running. Closes pnpm/pnpm#17530.

The `node` shim installs the pinned runtime with `hardened_install_config`. That config already turns off scripts, overrides, `packageExtensions`, catalogs, and patches, but it still loaded the global pnpmfile. The hook worker starts as bare `node`, and on `PATH` that is the same unprovisioned shim. So every level re-entered provisioning, waited on the slot lock, installed privately, and spawned another worker.

The fix sets `ignore_pnpmfile` in `hardened_install_config`. Shared and private runtime installs both go through it. Project installs still run the global pnpmfile, on the pinned Node.

This takes over pnpm/pnpm#17531 by @lazerg, who wrote the fix, the test, and the changeset. Their commit is imported unchanged with its authorship. On top of it, this PR adds an integration test, lists pnpmfile hooks in the function's doc comment, and names pnpm as the actor in the changeset. Thanks to `aron-intframe` for the source trace on the issue.

pnpm v11 is not affected. It has no global shims and loads pnpmfiles in-process.

prs.title: fix(install): link the runtime after a --no-runtime install
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Related to pnpm/pnpm#17542. The repeat-install fast path did not record the `runtime` setting, so after `pnpm install --no-runtime` a plain `pnpm install` reported "Already up to date" and never linked the runtime. The workspace state now records `runtime` while it is off, and the install gate treats a change as drift, so `skip_runtimes` moves from `Unseen` to `Recorded` in the settings classification.

The run gate ignores the new key, like it ignores `dev`/`optional`/`production`. Otherwise `pnpm run` after `pnpm install --no-runtime` would install again and link the runtime, which is the opposite of what the flag is for. When a passing run check refreshes the state, it keeps the recorded `runtime` the same way it keeps the dependency groups, so a later plain install still sees the change.

pnpm v11 had the same gap: `runtime` was not in `WORKSPACE_STATE_SETTING_KEYS`. It is now recorded there, an unset value reads as `true`, and `pnpm run`/`pnpm exec` ignore it. v11 already carries ignored settings forward when the run gate rewrites the state. Both CLIs write the same `runtime` key.

This is a partial fix. `pnpm install --no-runtime` on a project that already has the runtime linked now runs a full install, but that install still leaves `node_modules/.bin/node` in place, the same as `--no-runtime --frozen-lockfile` does today. Only `--force` removes it.

prs.title: perf: reuse the store verifier's mode reading for hardlinks and gate benchmark syscall counts
prs.author: jclaveau
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17543.

pnpm/pnpm#17502 stopped re-statting a store file shared by several packages, but every store file is still stat'ed once before its first hardlink. The store verifier (`check_pkg_files_integrity`) read that same inode's mode a moment earlier in the same install. On the vitest fixture, 12.17.0 makes about 100k `statx` calls per offline install, against 54k in 12.7.0.

This PR has two parts. They can be split into two PRs if you prefer:

1. **The fix.** The verifier records the mode it reads in a process-wide map keyed by store path (`pnpm_fs::file_mode`), and `source_has_desired_mode` stats only on a miss. A store file that fails verification has its entry marked stale, because its re-fetch may land a new inode with another mode. A verifier read only fills a path the map does not know yet, so a read that predates another thread's failure cannot bring the old mode back. Only the importer's own `stat` refills a stale entry. The map replaces pnpm/pnpm#17502's `DashSet` of linkable paths. `store_inode_mode_is_linkable` is unchanged, so the pnpm/pnpm#3807 semantics are unchanged.
2. **A syscall-count check in the integrated benchmark.** Wall time did not catch the 12.8.0 regression: each extra warm-cache `statx` costs about a microsecond, so the extra calls stayed inside the 5% noise allowance. The benchmark now runs each install twice more under `strace --summary-only` and fails when HEAD makes more file syscalls than main by more than max(2%, 5

## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17542. pnpm/pnpm#17545 fixed one direction of the issue: a plain install after `--no-runtime` now links the runtime. This PR fixes the other: `pnpm install --no-runtime` on a project whose runtime an earlier install linked now removes `node_modules/node` and its bin.

Three gates kept the runtime linked:

1. **The early up-to-date check** (`finished_via_install_fast_path`) runs before the install pipeline applies `--no-runtime` to the config. It compared the workspace state against `runtime` still on and reported "Already up to date". The flag is now applied to the fast-path config too, through the same `record_no_runtime_flag`.
2. **The frozen-tree up-to-date check** compared the current lockfile with the full wanted lockfile. Under `skip_runtimes`, `materialized_shape_matches` now leaves the direct runtimes out of the wanted shape, the way the install does when it writes the current lockfile. A tree that still holds the runtime no longer matches. A repeated `--no-runtime` install now matches and settles on this check, where before it re-materialized every time.
3. **The stale-link prune** (`PruneStaleModules`) treated every direct dependency of the wanted lockfile as wanted. That included one the install skips, so the old `node_modules/node` link survived even `--no-runtime --force`.
